title: The countdown kettle
prompt:
The shop kettle counts down before it whistles. Write `kettle(n)` so `kettle(3)` prints `3...`, `2...`, `1...` and then `Tea!`, each on its own line. Use recursion: `kettle` calls `kettle` with a smaller number. No loops.

When it works, `python3 kettle.py` prints those four lines.
hints: Two cases. When `n` is 0 or less, the kettle is done. Otherwise there is still counting to do.
The base case is `if n <= 0:` followed by `print("Tea!")`. In the other case, print `n` with three dots after it, using an f-string such as `f"{n}..."`.
After printing `n`, call `kettle(n - 1)`. That call does the rest of the countdown.
explain_after: This is the countdown from Think Python with a shop twist: the function prints `n` and calls itself with `n - 1`, and stops when `n` reaches 0 or goes below it [py-139]. The call with `n` equal to 0 is the base case [py-140]. Without it, the calls would never stop, and Python would end the program with a `RecursionError` [py-141].
